verified_claims_summary: Ottoni et al. was published in Social Science & Medicine in 2016 and used one-on-one seated and walk-along interviews with adults aged 60以上 living in three adjacent Vancouver neighborhoods, with n=28 in 2012 and n=22 in 2014. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27669123/?utm_source=openai))

The Ottoni study found that benches enhanced participants’ use and enjoyment of green and blue spaces, functioned as mobility aids, and contributed to social cohesion and social capital. “Benches become like porches” is the paper’s actual title and reflects its reported social findings. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27669123/?utm_source=openai))

Boavida et al.’s 2023 Geriatrics review analyzed 28 articles from 2020–2023. It reports preferences for more benches for relaxation and identifies maintained parks, seating, pleasant paths, toilets and cafés as factors encouraging older visitors. It also recommends user participation, observation and objective measures such as comfort and usability when evaluating bench design. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10606855/?utm_source=openai))

Swedish Radio reported the Triangeln-station discrimination complaint on March 4, 2011. Malmö’s project manager said the benches had arrived with an unexpectedly severe slope and that corrected prototypes and alterations to the remaining benches were planned; subsequent reporting says they were straightened after the station opened. ([sverigesradio.se](https://www.sverigesradio.se/artikel/4382816?utm_source=openai))

In February 2021, the official NYC Transit account stated that benches had been removed to prevent homeless people from sleeping on them. The post was deleted, and an MTA spokesperson said it had been posted in error while declining to confirm the reason or extent of removals. The article therefore correctly avoids presenting the post as proof of a formal systemwide policy. ([gothamist.com](https://gothamist.com/news/mta-deletes-tweet-explaining-why-subway-station-benches-were-removed?utm_source=openai))
